games.title: Reading Detective
games.description: Use unit evidence to solve each reading clue.

rounds.prompt: What lesson does the story of Dina the weaver begin to teach?
choices: That guarding your skill or knowledge only for yourself, like a well kept from everyone, can leave you helpless when trouble finally comes.
Because training makes the heart stronger and more efficient, so it pumps more blood with each beat and works less hard at rest.
That money is only a tool, and what really counts is making wise, balanced choices such as saving, budgeting and sharing with others.
rounds.answer: That guarding your skill or knowledge only for yourself, like a well kept from everyone, can leave you helpless when trouble finally comes.
rounds.explanation: Zane warns that a river which shares nothing becomes a swamp, and the storm then destroys everything Dina had guarded alone.

rounds.prompt: Which detail shows how proud Dina was of her weaving skill?
choices: Your performance will deteriorate over time, because your body lacks the fuel it needs to perform well.
One part for saving, one part for spending on needs or things you enjoy, and one part for giving to charity or helping your family.
She always refused to teach the younger women, saying her secret knowledge was the very thing that made her cloth valuable.
rounds.answer: She always refused to teach the younger women, saying her secret knowledge was the very thing that made her cloth valuable.
rounds.explanation: The passage says she guarded her methods closely and would not share her techniques with anyone.

rounds.prompt: What does the sport passage say happens if you do not eat enough healthy food?
choices: Both suggest that hoarding selfishly, whether it is weaving skill or money, is unwise, and that sharing with others makes a person stronger.
Your performance will deteriorate over time, because your body lacks the fuel it needs to perform well.
As a community of living things that depend on each other and on the land, water and air around them.
rounds.answer: Your performance will deteriorate over time, because your body lacks the fuel it needs to perform well.
rounds.explanation: The writer links a balanced diet of fruit, vegetables and whole grains to having the energy to train and compete.

rounds.prompt: What overall point does the inventions text make about who can invent?
choices: That anyone with curiosity, creativity and commitment can invent, because the real procedure is to observe, question, experiment and improve.
As a community of living things that depend on each other and on the land, water and air around them.
It reminds me to share my ideas and sources openly instead of guarding them, so my work grows rather than turning stale like a swamp.
rounds.answer: That anyone with curiosity, creativity and commitment can invent, because the real procedure is to observe, question, experiment and improve.
rounds.explanation: The passage ends by saying young inventors in Kenya and Somalia solved real problems without big laboratories or money.

rounds.prompt: What is the central message of the Money Matters text?
choices: That anyone with curiosity, creativity and commitment can invent, because the real procedure is to observe, question, experiment and improve.
That guarding your skill or knowledge only for yourself, like a well kept from everyone, can leave you helpless when trouble finally comes.
That money is only a tool, and what really counts is making wise, balanced choices such as saving, budgeting and sharing with others.
rounds.answer: That money is only a tool, and what really counts is making wise, balanced choices such as saving, budgeting and sharing with others.
rounds.explanation: The passage repeats that money is not good or bad on its own; how we use it is what matters.

rounds.prompt: The weaver story and the money text both value wisdom; what shared idea about sharing do they express?
choices: She always refused to teach the younger women, saying her secret knowledge was the very thing that made her cloth valuable.
Both suggest that hoarding selfishly, whether it is weaving skill or money, is unwise, and that sharing with others makes a person stronger.
It made books far cheaper and quicker to produce, so within decades millions who had never owned a book could finally read and learn.
rounds.answer: Both suggest that hoarding selfishly, whether it is weaving skill or money, is unwise, and that sharing with others makes a person stronger.
rounds.explanation: Dina's guarded well fails her, while the money passage praises budgeting and giving to charity.

games.title: Memory Pairs
games.description: Reveal tiles and connect each word with its meaning.

pairs: certainty
Being sure that something is true.
clause
A group of words containing a verb, part of a sentence.
inference
A conclusion you reach from clues rather than being told.
reference
A mention of where information came from.
apostrophe
A mark showing a missing letter or who owns something.
income
The money a person earns from working or selling things.
employment
Having paid work, or the work itself.
hygiene
Keeping yourself and your surroundings clean in order to stay healthy.
flood
A great overflow of water onto normally dry land.
instrument
A tool or device used to make music or to carry out a particular job.
treacherous
Dangerous and unsafe, often because a place is not what it first seems.
caravan
A group of people and animals travelling together, often across a wide desert.
script
The written words of a play, film or speech that performers learn and say.
excavation
The careful digging of the ground to uncover buildings, bones or buried objects.
hypothesise
To suggest an explanation that can then be tested.
theorise
To form an idea that explains a set of facts.
coefficient
The number placed in front of a letter in algebra.
outcome
The result of something, or one possible result in probability.
